issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add five DeepSeek V4 nightly configurations for Model Runner V2:

- Flash single-node
- Flash PD-prefix
- Pro DSpark PD-prefix
- Pro DSpark 1M-PD
- Pro MTP PD-prefix

The PR also prevents the Chinese Read the Docs build from resolving tools/bisect instead of Python standard-library bisect when tools/generate_zh_docs.py is executed directly. This fixes the deterministic ImportError reported by build 34403297.

This PR supersedes #15765. GitHub does not permit reopening that PR after its force-pushed head branch was closed. The MRV2 slot-mapping runtime fix remains separate in #15817.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No.

### How was this patch tested?

- All five configurations passed their configured smoke, accuracy, and/or performance validation.
- Flash single-node GPQA: 88.89; three-run performance mean: 234.6171 requests/s.
- Flash PD-prefix AIME: 96.67.
- Pro DSpark PD-prefix AIME: 93.33; three-run performance mean: 471.8498 requests/s.
- Pro DSpark 1M-PD three-run performance mean: 16.9460 requests/s.
- Pro MTP PD-prefix AIME: 93.33; three-run performance mean: 471.1520 requests/s.
- Verified the Read the Docs failure mode with tools/ first on sys.path; after the fix, random imports the standard-library bisect.py module.
- git diff --check passes.

issues.title: [Feature] DSpark expert-pool routing for the expert-offload path
issues.body:
> **Stacked on #18604.** This branch contains #18604's expert-offload commits plus the expert-pool increment. Review only the commits after `fc2d40a`; the file delta is `git diff fc2d40a...dspark-expert-pool-fusion`. Merge after #18604. Supersedes #21594 and #21680 (kernel and integration base from #21680; graph coverage, hardware accuracy test, and operator documentation from #21594).

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DSpark speculative decoding verifies draft tokens block by block, and every row in a verify block currently routes through the MoE router independently: each row performs its own full top-k expert selection. Rows within one verify block are highly correlated and their expert choices overlap heavily, so per-row independent routing activates more distinct experts than the block actually needs, lowering the expert hit rate on the offload path and adding fused-MoE dispatch cost.

This PR adds opt-in expert-pool routing (L routing) to the ModelRunner V2 single-device expert-offload path:

- **Shared candidate pool.** For each request, the first `protected_positions` verification rows (anchor included) contribute their Top-6 experts; each remaining row contributes `suffix_experts` candidates. Every suffix row still selects six experts from the batch union (same scoring, same lowest-expert-ID tie-break as native routing), so the activation footprint of a verify block shrinks toward what its anchors actually need.
- **Two Triton kernels.** One kernel builds the candidate pool from staged token roles; a second returns logical expert IDs and normalized weights to the existing offload path.
- **Graph safety.** Routing state is staged into persistent buffers each step, so eager execution and ACL graph capture/replay observe the same contract. Full verification-width graphs record a merged routing sequence (fused route + native router + merge) whose per-row behavior is driven by the staged roles, so structured-output steps, rejected-draft steps, and batches mixing in prefilling requests also replay the captured graph; mixed (non-uniform) and short-draft batches still run eager.
- **Opt-in and guarded.** `dspark_expert_pool` is disabled by default and validates its contract at startup (requires enabled expert offload and DSpark with a positive draft-token count; `protected_positions` within the verify width; `suffix_experts` within `[0, Top-K]`).
- Unit coverage (19 cases: request boundaries, draft counts, padding, role refresh, graph eligibility, native routing outputs) plus a nightly e2e accuracy test and operator documentation.

Measured on a single Ascend 950PR NPU card (deepseek-v4-flash-0731, DSpark speculative decoding) with a semantically equivalent implementation of the same routing contract on the predecessor branch (#21594); re-measurement on this branch is recommended before merge:

| Batch size | Output throughput (rel. to baseline) | Mean accepted length (baseline → pool) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | +21.0% | 4.17 → 3.99 |
| 2 | +29.5% | 4.18 → 4.35 |
| 4 | +27.8% | 3.99 → 3.91 |

Accuracy, deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (same predecessor measurement):

| Benchmark | Baseline | Expert-pool routing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K | 94.8 | 94.4 |
| GPQA | 79.8 | 80.3 |
| HumanEval | 93.3 | 92.1 |
| AIME 2026 | 93.3 | 93.3 |
| LongBench-V2 | 39.2 | 41.6 |

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can enable expert-pool routing through `--additional-config`:

```json
{
  "expert_offload_config": {"enabled": true, "num_device_experts": 84},
  "dspark_expert_pool": {"enabled": true, "protected_positions": 2, "suffix_experts": 0}
}
```

The feature is disabled by default; when it is disabled or not configured, routing behavior is unchanged. `protected_positions` includes the anchor, and `suffix_experts` controls how many candidates each suffix row contributes. See the configuration reference and speculative-decoding feature guide for a full serving example.

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit coverage in `tests/ut/expert_offload/test_dspark_expert_pool.py` (19 cases: request boundaries, draft counts, padding, role refresh, graph eligibility, native routing outputs in mixed batches).
- Nightly e2e kernel-accuracy test `tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_dspark_expert_pool.py` compares the fused kernels against an embedded pure-torch reference (exact expert IDs, documented weight tolerance) on NPU, including padding-row isolation.
- Operator documentation in `vllm_ascend/ops/triton/docs/deepseek_expert_pool.md` per the Triton description specification.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `python -m py_compile`, and `git diff --check` pass for all changed files.

### Checklist

- Testing
  - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: routing request boundaries, draft counts, padding rows, and role refresh are covered.
  - [x] **Regression test**: not applicable; this PR adds a new opt-in feature and is disabled by default.
  - [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: startup configuration validation (offload enabled, DSpark contract, position/suffix ranges) is covered.
  - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: unit tests plus nightly NPU kernel-accuracy test against a torch reference.
  - [x] **Performance impact**: output throughput +21.0% / +29.5% / +27.8% at batch size 1 / 2 / 4 on a single Ascend 950PR card (tables above).

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58

issues.title: [Feature][MoE] Support anchor-union activation routing for DSpark and DFlash speculative decoding
issues.body:
> **Stacked on #18604.** This branch contains #18604's expert-offload commits plus the activation-routing increment. Review only the commits after `fc2d40a` (`feat(moe): integrate activation routing with MRv2` onward); the 12-file delta is `git diff fc2d40a...activation-routing-mrv2`. Merge after #18604.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

DSpark and DFlash speculative decoding verify draft tokens block by block, and every row in a verify block currently routes through the MoE router independently: each row performs its own full top-k expert selection. Rows within one verify block are highly correlated and their expert choices overlap heavily, so per-row independent routing ends up activating more distinct experts than the block actually needs. The larger activated-expert working set lowers the expert hit rate and adds fused-MoE dispatch cost.

This PR adds anchor-union activation routing for Model Runner V2, so verify rows share one expert pool and shrink the activation footprint:

- **Anchor-union routing.** Anchor rows keep their own top-k experts. Suffix rows are restricted to the union of the anchor selections across the padded verify batch (a single verify block in the common single-request case), and the restricted routing result is applied before fused MoE dispatch.
- **Reference and fused-native implementations.** A graph-safe reference implementation covers all supported contracts; the fused-native kernel path accelerates the validated DeepSeek DSpark contract (FP32, 256 experts, Top-6, sqrtsoftplus). Expert IDs agree exactly for tie-free inputs; weights agree within the tolerances documented in the operator docs.
- **Graph safety.** Routing roles and state are prepared on the host into persistent buffers each step, so eager execution and ACL graph capture/replay observe the same contract.
- **Config assembly.** The `activation_routing` section derives DSpark/DFlash defaults from the engine and model configuration, so the feature needs no hand-tuned values in the common case.
- Unit coverage for routing state, segment boundaries, and configuration validation.

Measured on a single Ascend 950PR NPU card (deepseek-v4-flash-0731, DFlash speculative decoding):

| Batch size | Output throughput (rel. to baseline) | Mean accepted length (baseline → activation) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | +21.0% | 4.17 → 3.99 |
| 2 | +29.5% | 4.18 → 4.35 |
| 4 | +27.8% | 3.99 → 3.91 |

Accuracy, deepseek-v4-flash-0731:

| Benchmark | Baseline | Activation routing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GSM8K | 94.8 | 94.4 |
| GPQA | 79.8 | 80.3 |
| HumanEval | 93.3 | 92.1 |
| AIME 2026 | 93.3 | 93.3 |
| LongBench-V2 | 39.2 | 41.6 |

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Users can enable activation routing through `--additional-config`:

```json
{
  "activation_routing": {
    "enabled": true,
    "backend": "anchor_union_fused_native"
  }
}
```

The feature is disabled by default. When it is disabled or not configured, the existing routing behavior is preserved. With the fused-native backend, the DeepSeek DSpark contract uses the fused kernels; other contracts fall back to the reference implementation (the Top-8 BF16 fused path is reserved for a follow-up PR).

### How was this patch tested?

- Unit coverage in `tests/ut/test_dflash_anchor_state.py` (routing state, segment boundaries, configuration validation, softmax-contract fallback to the reference path); `python -m py_compile` and `git diff --check` pass for all changed files.
- End-to-end validation on a single Ascend 950PR NPU card with the throughput and accuracy tables above.

### Checklist

- Testing
  - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: routing segment boundaries and state transitions are covered.
  - [x] **Regression test**: not applicable; this PR adds a new opt-in feature.
  - [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: configuration and backend validation paths are covered.
  - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: added unit tests for routing state behavior.
  - [x] **Performance impact**: output throughput +21.0% / +29.5% / +27.8% at batch size 1 / 2 / 4 on a single Ascend 950PR card (tables above).

issues.title: [RFC]: Ascend supports Gemma4 model and W8A8 quantization guidance.
issues.body:
### Motivation.

On April 2, Google released a new open-source model called Gemma4. As a multimodal understanding model, it can process inputs such as text, images, videos, and audio, and generate text outputs. Gemma4 performs excellently in the Arena benchmark, offers high cost-effectiveness, and supports 128K and 256K context lengths, making it highly suitable for scenarios such as inference, agent workflows, coding, and multimodal understanding.

The deployment scenarios cover a wide range of environments, from mobile devices and edge devices (E2B, E4B) to consumer-grade NPUs and workstations (26BA4B, 31B). It can be deployed in various settings, from high-end smartphones to laptops and servers, enabling more people to access cutting-edge AI.

### Proposed Change.

- Support FullAttention with Large Head (up to 512 dim) on vLLM-Ascend by implementing fallback to `npu_fusion_attention` for prefill when head_size exceeds FIA TND supported sizes {64, 128, 192}
- Support KV Cache sharing mechanism between Local and Global attention layers with producer-consumer pattern and event synchronization
- Support Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with proper block_table handling during graph replay
- Make MoE custom routing compatible with functions that do not accept num_experts.
- Adjust Triton RoPE head tile size for TP-sharded small local head counts.
- Support multimodal input_ids handling for graph compilation when models consume inputs_embeds
- Add unit tests for Large Head attention fallback, KV sharing mechanism, and custom routing compatibility
- Add E2E tests with real Gemma4 weights (26B/31B, BF16/W8A8)

### Feedback Period.

issues.title: [RFC]: vllm-ascend-model-adapter — AI-Assisted Model Adaptation Skill
issues.body: # RFC: vllm-ascend-model-adapter — AI-Assisted Model Adaptation Skill - **Status**: Draft - **Date**: 2026-03-23 - **Authors**: vllm-ascend maintainers - **Scope**: AI agent skill design for adapting and validating models on Ascend NPU --- ## Abstract This RFC proposes a standardized AI agent skill — `vllm-ascend-model-adapter` — for adapting Hugging Face or local model checkpoints to run on Ascend NPU via `vllm-ascend`. The skill encodes the full adaptation lifecycle as a structured, reproducible 10-step playbook executed by an AI agent (Claude Code). It covers pre-flight analysis, Ascend compatibility gating, implementation, two-stage hardware validation, feature verification, and delivery of documentation and a signed commit. The goal is to make model adaptation faster, more consistent, and accessible to contributors who are unfamiliar with Ascend-specific pitfalls. ### Overview --- > update on 2026.05.11 23:24:42: we should fix some steps instead of using the llm all over the progress. Thus we fix the steps of env check, model type classification and the basic test into fixed scripts > --- ## Motivation ### Problem Adding support for a new model on Ascend NPU currently requires: 1. Deep familiarity with vLLM's internal architecture (registry, weight loader, attention backend, etc.). 2. Knowledge of Ascend-specific constraints (no CUDA operators, fp8 dequantization, ACLGraph behavior, KV-head replication under TP, etc.). 3. Ability to triage a wide range of runtime failures with limited documentation. 4. Manual writing of test configs, tutorial docs, and analysis reports. This expertise is concentrated in a small number of engineers, creating a bottleneck when the community needs to onboard new models quickly (e.g., in response to upstream vLLM adding support for a new architecture). ### Goal Encode the adaptation process as a machine-executable skill so that: - An AI agent can execute the full adaptation workflow autonomously. - Human engineers review outputs rather than performing every step manually. - The process is deterministic and auditable — every decision is backed by evidence. - New contributors can trigger the skill with minimal background knowledge. --- ## Design ### Skill overview The skill is stored under `.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/` and consists of: ```text SKILL.md ← machine-readable playbook (agent entry point) readme.md ← human-readable usage guide references/ workflow-checklist.md ← step-by-step shell commands multimodal-ep-aclgraph-lessons.md ← feature validation patterns fp8-on-npu-lessons.md ← fp8 dequantization guide troubleshooting.md ← failure signatures and resolutions deliverables.md ← required outputs and commit discipline ``` The agent reads `SKILL.md` as its primary instruction set. Reference files are consulted at specific points in the workflow. ### Execution environment All implementation and validation is performed inside the official `vllm-ascend` Docker container at fixed paths: | Path | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `/vllm-workspace/vllm` | vLLM source (editable install) | | `/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend` | vllm-ascend source (editable install) | | `/workspace` | Working directory for `vllm serve` | | `/models/` | Model checkpoint root | The runtime import source is verified at the start of every session: ```bash python -c "import vllm; print(vllm.__file__)" # Must point to /vllm-workspace/vllm/... ``` ### 10-step playbook #### Step 1 — Collect context The agent confirms the model path, implementation roots, delivery repo, and the default feature set to validate: - **All models**: ACLGraph - **MoE models only**: EP (expert parallel), flashcomm1 - **VL models only**: multimodal (text+image inference) - **Checkpoint-dependent**: MTP (validated only when the checkpoint explicitly supports it, determined in Step 2) User requirements extend this baseline; they do not replace it. #### Step 2 — Analyze model The agent inspects `config.json`, modeling files, processor files, tokenizer, and the safetensors weight index. **Model type classification** is performed first: ```text LLM ─┬─ Standard full attention ├─ Sliding window attention ├─ Mamba (SSM) ├─ Multi-latent attention (MLA) └─ Hybrid (e.g. MLA + Mamba layers interleaved) VLM ─── Vision-language model (vision encoder + language backbone) Whisper ─ Encoder-decoder ASR model ``` The model type determines which validation steps apply and which features are non-applicable. Additional analysis: - Architecture class and whether it already exists in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py`. - Attention variant (GQA / MQA / MHA / MLA / sliding window). - Quantization type (fp8, fp4, or none). - State-dict key prefix layout (for weight remap planning). #### Step 3 — Operator compatibility gate The agent scans the model code for new operators and classifies them by type. This step acts as an early-exit gate: | Operator type | Ascend compatibility | Action | | --- | --- | --- | | **Torch** (native PyTorch) | ✅ Functional | Note performance uncertainty in report | | **Triton** kernel | ⚠️ Uncertain | Verify functional correctness and accuracy on Ascend | | **CUDA** kernel with fallback | ❌ CUDA unsupported | Use fallback path; document it | | **CUDA** kernel, no fallback | ❌ Blocked | **Early exit: file GitHub issue, skip all validation** | | **Triton** kernel, verification fails | ❌ Blocked | **Early exit: file GitHub issue, skip all validation** | **CUDA early-exit rule**: If any operator is a pure CUDA kernel with no Torch/Triton alternative, the agent stops immediately and files a GitHub issue documenting: - which operator blocks Ascend support, - why no fallback exists, - recommended path forward (e.g., implement a custom Ascend op in `vllm-ascend`). **Triton early-exit rule**: If a Triton kernel is verified to be non-functional on Ascend (correctness failure or unacceptable accuracy degradation), the agent stops and files a GitHub issue documenting: - which Triton kernel fails and the observed failure mode, - recommended path forward (e.g., replace with a Torch-native fallback or implement a custom Ascend op). Both early-exit gates avoid investing engineering time in architecture adaptation for a model that cannot run correctly on Ascend until the blocking operator issue is resolved. #### Step 4 — Framework-side code analysis Beyond the model file and operators, upstream vLLM commits often touch framework modules (scheduler, attention backend, sampler, weight loader, worker). The agent identifies these changes and determines whether `vllm-ascend` needs to respond: ```text Changed vLLM framework module │ ├─ Already patched/overridden by vllm-ascend? │ └─ YES → Check if the existing patch still applies correctly │ after the upstream change. Update if needed; │ otherwise no further action is needed. │ └─ NOT covered + contains Ascend-incompatible logic? └─ YES → Add minimal override under /vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend/ ``` Framework-side patches are kept minimal and scoped to incompatible code paths only. #### Step 5 — Choose adaptation strategy | Situation | Strategy | | --- | --- | | Architecture exists and is compatible | Reuse; patch only what's broken | | Architecture missing or incompatible | Implement new adapter | | Remote code needs newer `transformers` symbols | Copy required files — never upgrade `transformers` | | Failure requires modeling code in `vllm-ascend` | **Do not proceed** — raise a GitHub issue to analyze the root cause | **New adapter implementation checklist:** 1. `vllm/model_executor/models/.py` — model class and weight loader 2. `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/.py` — multimodal processor (VL only) 3. `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` — architecture name registration 4. Explicit weight remap rules: qkv sharding, QK/KV norms, RoPE variants, fp8 scale pairing #### Step 6 — Implement minimal code changes (vLLM source only) All model adaptation code is implemented in `/vllm-workspace/vllm` only. Model-specific files and patches must never be introduced in `/vllm-workspace/vllm-ascend` — if a model cannot function on Ascend without that, the skill raises a GitHub issue instead of proceeding. Weight mapping is explicit and auditable. No unrelated refactors. ```bash python -m py_compile /vllm-workspace/vllm/vllm/model_executor/models/.py ``` #### Step 7 — Two-stage validation on Ascend This is the core quality gate. **Both stages are required.** Dummy-only evidence is never sufficient for sign-off. **Stage A — Dummy fast gate** ```bash vllm serve /models/ \ --load-format dummy \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --tensor-parallel-size \ --max-model-len 131072 \ --max-num-seqs 16 \ --port 8000 ``` Purpose: rapidly validate architecture path, operator path, and API path without loading real weights. ACLGraph evidence is also collected here. > `Application startup complete` alone is **not** a pass. A smoke inference request is mandatory immediately after startup. **Stage B — Real-weight mandatory gate** Same command, minus `--load-format dummy`. Purpose: validate real-only risks — weight key mapping, fp8/fp4 dequantization path, KV/QK norm sharding with real tensor shapes, load-time/runtime stability. > Stage B **cannot be skipped**. A model is not considered adapted until real-weight inference produces HTTP 200 with non-empty output. #### Step 8 — Validate inference and features Minimum smoke sequence: ```bash # 1. Readiness check curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models # 2. Text inference (all models) curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"say hi"}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":16}' # 3. Text+image inference (VL models only) ``` Feature status is reported using four categories: | Symbol | Meaning | | --- | --- | | ✅ | Supported and verified | | ❌ | Framework-level unsupported | | ⚠️ | Checkpoint missing (feature not present in this model's weights/config) | | N/A | Not applicable (e.g., EP on a dense model) | Capacity baseline: `max-model-len=128k` + `max-num-seqs=16`. Extended concurrency (32/64) validated if requested. > **Note**: Accuracy evaluation and performance benchmarking are out of scope for this skill. They are handled by a dedicated separate skill that should be invoked after this skill completes. #### Step 9 — Backport, generate artifacts, commit 1. Backport minimal diff from `/vllm-workspace/*` to the delivery repo. 2. Generate `tests/e2e/models/configs/.yaml` with accuracy metrics. 3. Generate `docs/source/tutorials/models/.md` following the standard template. 4. Update `docs/source/tutorials/models/index.md`. 5. Deliver exactly one signed commit: `git commit -sm "..."`. #### Step 10 — Handoff artifacts The final response includes (all in Chinese, compact): - **Analysis report**: architecture summary, incompatibility root causes, code changes, feature status matrix, dummy-vs-real validation matrix, theoretical vs practical max-model-len, fallback ladder evidence. - **Runbook**: server startup command, validation curl commands, eager/TorchDynamo fallbacks. - SKILL.md summary posted as a comment on the originating GitHub issue. --- ## Key design decisions and rationale ### Decision 1: operator gate as an explicit early-exit step **Problem**: Engineers have invested days adapting an architecture only to discover a blocking CUDA or non-functional Triton kernel with no Ascend alternative. **Decision**: Make operator classification a mandatory step before any code is written. CUDA-only operators with no fallback exit immediately. Triton kernels must pass functional verification on Ascend before the workflow continues. **Rationale**: Failing fast saves engineering time and surfaces hardware gaps to the community early. ### Decision 2: dummy-first, real-weight mandatory **Problem**: Running with real weights takes significantly longer and requires the checkpoint to be available. But dummy runs can miss real-only failures (weight key mismatches, fp8 scale pairing, KV norm shape errors under TP). **Decision**: Two-stage approach — dummy fast gate for architecture/operator validation, real-weight gate mandatory before sign-off. **Rationale**: Speed (dummy) and correctness (real) are both required. Neither alone is sufficient. ### Decision 3: feature-first validation (ACLGraph + EP before eager) **Problem**: Eager mode always works but doesn't represent production deployment. Discovering graph capture failures only after shipping a tutorial is wasteful. **Decision**: Try ACLGraph + EP as the primary validation path. Eager mode is used only as an isolation fallback. **Rationale**: If a model is delivered with a tutorial that defaults to eager mode because graph mode was never tried, that tutorial will perform poorly in production. ### Decision 4: framework-side code analysis before adaptation **Problem**: Upstream vLLM commits often modify framework modules (not just model files) that vllm-ascend has patched. Without reviewing these changes, vllm-ascend overrides can silently break. **Decision**: Explicitly analyze all changed framework modules and check vllm-ascend coverage before writing any model code. **Rationale**: Prevents silent regressions in existing adapted models caused by untracked framework-level drift. ### Decision 5: minimal patch scope, no modeling code in vllm-ascend **Problem**: Over-broad patches create maintenance debt and increase the risk of regressions when upstream vLLM changes. Historically, modeling files or patches introduced into `vllm-ascend` become orphaned and hard to maintain as the model's upstream vLLM support evolves. **Decision**: All model adaptation code belongs in `/vllm-workspace/vllm`. Never introduce modeling files or patches into `vllm-ascend`. If a model cannot function on Ascend without such a patch, stop and raise a GitHub issue to analyze the root cause. **Rationale**: Keeps `vllm-ascend` focused on Ascend platform compatibility (framework-level overrides) rather than per-model logic. Reduces forward-compatibility risk and makes upstream rebase easier. --- ## Failure handling: the fallback ladder When startup or inference fails, the agent follows a strict ordered ladder before modifying code: ```text 1. Reproduce once to confirm a deterministic failure signature ↓ 2. Add --enforce-eager → isolate graph-capture vs. operator failures ↓ 3. [VL] TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1 → isolate dynamo/interpolate/contiguous failures ↓ 4. [VL] --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0,"audio":0}' → isolate multimodal processor failures from model core failures ↓ 5. Apply targeted code fix, loop back to Stage A ``` This ordered approach ensures that each code change addresses a confirmed failure rather than a hypothesis. ### Known failure signatures and resolutions | Failure | Root cause | Resolution | | --- | --- | --- | | `fp8 quantization is currently not supported in npu` | fp8 execution kernels absent on Ascend | Dequantize fp8→bf16 at load time using `weight` + `weight_scale_inv` pairing | | Shape mismatch `128 vs 64` under TP | KV-head replication not handled | Detect replicated KV heads; use local norm-shard path | | ACLGraph `507903` capture error | Stream capture sequence invalidated | Set `HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV`; reduce `--max-model-len` | | HCCL bind error on startup | Stale server holding port 8000 | Kill stale processes; free port before retry | | `AtbRingMLA` runtime error after startup | MLA backend/rope implementation mismatch | Eager isolation; check vllm-ascend MLA/rope implementation | | `torch._dynamo` + `interpolate` + NPU contiguous | TorchDynamo compiles interpolate against CUDA semantics | Add `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1` as fallback; investigate code-level fix | | `skip_tensor_conversion` signature mismatch | Processor API version mismatch between HF remote code and current transformers | Text-only isolation to separate processor layer from model core; align processor implementation | | `Cannot copy out of meta tensor` | Meta tensor load path triggered unexpectedly after MM isolation | Treat as secondary failure; return to code-fix path | --- ## Deliverables specification Every adaptation produces the following artifacts in the delivery repo: ### Code - Minimal diff covering only the target model's adapter, processor (if VL), registry entry, and weight remap rules. - All code changes are in `/vllm-workspace/vllm` only; no modeling files or patches in `vllm-ascend`. - Exactly one signed commit: `git commit -sm "feat: add support on Ascend NPU"`. ### Test config Path: `tests/e2e/models/configs/.yaml` Required fields: `model_name` (HF path), `hardware`, `tasks` (list with `name`, `metrics` containing `name` + `value`), `num_fewshot`. Values populated from real evaluation results. ### Tutorial doc Path: `docs/source/tutorials/models/.md` Required sections: Introduction, Supported Features, Environment Preparation (docker tabs for A2/A3), Deployment (serve script), Functional Verification (curl example), Accuracy Evaluation, Performance. `docs/source/tutorials/models/index.md` updated to include the new entry. ### Analysis report (Chinese, compact) - Architecture summary and model type classification - Operator compatibility findings (including any Triton verification results) - Framework-side changes and vllm-ascend coverage assessment - Code changes and rationale - Feature status matrix (✅ / ❌ / ⚠️ / N/A for ACLGraph, EP, flashcomm1, multimodal; MTP included if checkpoint supports it) - Dummy-vs-real validation matrix with explicit non-equivalence notes - Theoretical max-model-len (from config) vs practical max-model-len (from hardware) - Fallback ladder evidence (which fallbacks were tried, what each revealed) ### Runbook (Chinese, compact) - Server startup command (default: ACLGraph + real weights, port 8000) - Validation curl commands - Eager mode and TorchDynamo fallback commands (where applicable) --- ## Quality gate — mandatory before sign-off All of the following must be true before the skill declares success: - [ ] `vllm serve` starts from `/workspace` on port 8000 - [ ] `GET /v1/models` returns HTTP 200 - [ ] At least one text inference request returns HTTP 200 with non-empty output - [ ] VL models: at least one text+image request returns HTTP 200 with non-empty output - [ ] ACLGraph / EP / flashcomm1 / multimodal all reported with status; MTP reported if checkpoint supports it - [ ] `max-model-len=128k` + `max-num-seqs=16` capacity baseline reported (or explicit reason if infeasible) - [ ] Real-weight (Stage B) evidence is present — dummy-only is insufficient - [ ] `tests/e2e/models/configs/.yaml` exists with correct schema - [ ] `docs/source/tutorials/models/.md` exists with all required sections - [ ] `docs/source/tutorials/models/index.md` updated - [ ] Exactly one signed commit in the delivery repo - [ ] SKILL.md summary posted on the originating GitHub issue --- ## Alternatives considered ### Alternative A: document-only approach (wiki / confluence) A static wiki describing how to adapt models manually. Rejected because: - Does not eliminate the need for Ascend expertise. - Does not enforce consistency across adaptations. - Cannot self-update when new failure patterns are discovered. ### Alternative B: automated CI-only validation Run automated tests without AI-driven analysis. Rejected because: - Cannot make architectural decisions (new adapter vs reuse, weight remap strategy). - Cannot triage novel failures without a decision tree. - Cannot generate documentation. ### Alternative C: per-model custom scripts Write a bespoke adaptation script per model family. Rejected because: - Maintenance burden scales with number of models. - Expertise encoded in scripts rather than shared skill. ### Alternative D: separate skills per model type One skill for LLMs, one for VLMs, one for Whisper. Rejected because: - The core adaptation lifecycle is identical; only specific validation steps differ. - Branching logic within one skill is simpler than maintaining multiple skill entry points. --- ## Open questions 1. **Triton on Ascend**: Triton kernels are currently classified as "uncertain" on Ascend. Should we establish a dedicated Triton verification sub-workflow with specific accuracy benchmarks? 2. **Quantization beyond fp8**: fp4 models are beginning to appear. Should fp4 dequantization be treated the same as fp8, or does it require a separate path? 3. **Hybrid attention models**: The skill handles hybrid models as a sub-type of LLM. As models with 3+ attention types appear, does the classification need to become more structured? 4. **Custom Ascend op integration**: When the CUDA early-exit gate fires and an Ascend custom op is eventually implemented, what is the re-entry flow? Should the skill include a "resume from operator gate" path? 5. **Multi-node adaptation**: The current skill targets single-machine (A2/A3) setups. Multi-node EP validation is not covered. When should this be added? --- > update on 2026.05.11 23:24:42: we're planning to validate this skill on `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` and `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` --- --- ## References - [vllm-ascend repository](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend) - [vLLM model executor source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/main/vllm/model_executor/models) - [SKILL.md — agent entry point](.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/SKILL.md) - [readme.md — usage guide](.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/readme.md) - [workflow-checklist.md](.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/references/workflow-checklist.md) - [troubleshooting.md](.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/references/troubleshooting.md) - [fp8-on-npu-lessons.md](.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/references/fp8-on-npu-lessons.md) - [multimodal-ep-aclgraph-lessons.md](.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/references/multimodal-ep-aclgraph-lessons.md) - [deliverables.md](.agents/skills/vllm-ascend-model-adapter/references/deliverables.md)

issues.title: [Ops][Feature] Support online target LM head quantization with Model Runner V2
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Add online target LM head quantization independently of checkpoint-format dispatch. Model Runner V2 users can keep the checkpoint's floating-point output head or quantize it at load time without generating a new checkpoint.

- On A2/A3, convert FP16/BF16 LM head weights with `npu_dynamic_quant` and reuse the existing INT8 activation quantization, matmul, and NZ conversion path.
- On A5, select the registered MXFP8 head method and use `npu_dynamic_mx_quant`, 32-element E8M0 scales, and the existing MXFP8 matmul implementation.
- Quantize vocabulary rows in chunks to bound temporary allocations. Use the standard vocabulary-shard loader and retain floating-point bias.
- Support floating-point checkpoints, ModelSlim `FLOAT` heads, and explicitly excluded compressed-tensors heads. Preserve existing checkpoint methods for prequantized heads.
- Keep independently loaded draft heads unchanged. Upstream speculative loaders may still share the target head; their existing sharing behavior is preserved.
- Accept both `lm_head` and `head` output-head names, including nested prefixes. Reject shared embedding weights if either `hf_config` or `hf_text_config` enables `tie_word_embeddings`, and handle missing/`None` configuration objects safely.

The change uses the existing `AscendParallelLMHead`, `AscendEmbeddingMethod`, and quantization scheme registry. No model-runner changes or upstream patches are introduced.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

Yes. Set `--additional-config '{"lm_head_quantization":"w8a8_dynamic"}'` to enable online quantization of the target LM head. Omitting the option preserves checkpoint behavior. Model Runner V2 is required; 310P and tied embedding weights are not adapted by this change.

Documentation is added to `docs/source/user_guide/configuration/additional_config.md`, with release note fragment `release_notes/fragments/21706.yaml`.

### How was this patch tested?

**Unit tests and static checks**

- Focused CPU tests: **127 passed** using the existing test dependency image (Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.10, torch-npu 2.10, vLLM 0.32). The harness mocks NPU format conversion and disables plugin initialization; it does not establish NPU execution correctness.
- Covered files: `tests/ut/quantization/test_lm_head_quantization.py`, `test_method_adapters.py`, `methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_dynamic.py`, `methods/w8a8/test_w8a8_mxfp8.py`, and `methods/test_registry.py`.
- New regression cases cover `head`/`lm_head` and nested prefixes for target/draft roles, plus missing, `None`, false, and true values in both Hugging Face config locations.
- With the original selector restored in the same test process, the 24 new cases produced **8 failures and 16 passes**; the fixed selector passes all 24, reproducing both reviewed defects.
- Existing cases cover configuration errors, checkpoint dispatch, vocabulary shards, padding, FP16/BF16 weights, floating-point bias, repeated post-load processing, MX scale layout, chunk boundaries, and registry extension.
- `git diff --check`, Ruff lint/format, codespell, and Markdown lint checks passed. The local `bash format.sh ci` attempt timed out (exit 124) while installing actionlint; the remote **pre-commit CI passed**, including Gitleaks, the complete pre-commit run, and mypy for Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12. DCO and Markdown link checks also passed.

**Hardware and model accuracy validation (`af7182ce0`)**

- A2: 24 real NPU format/dtype/bias/shard cases, plus FP16/BF16 graph replay, passed. C-Eval validation with the standard loader: 1,144/1,346 (84.9926%).
- A5 (Ascend 950DT), Qwen3.6-27B-W8A8, TP4 on physical cards 4-7, Model Runner V2, eager, BF16 KV, MTP disabled: all four TP ranks confirmed MXFP8 weights and execution of `npu_dynamic_mx_quant` and `npu_quant_matmul`, with finite outputs.
- A5 C-Eval validation: BF16 head **1,135/1,346 (84.3239%)**; MXFP8 head **1,135/1,346 (84.3239%)**. No truncated outputs.
- A5 GPQA Diamond, 198 questions per group, one response per question, thinking enabled, concurrency 32, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `top_k=20`, `min_p=0`, `presence_penalty=0`, `repetition_penalty=1`, `seed=0`, `max_tokens=32768`, `max_model_len=131072`: raw scores **163/198 (82.32%)** for both heads. Applying the same Markdown-bold normalization to both groups corrects one missed BF16 answer: BF16 **164/198 (82.83%)**, MXFP8 **163/198 (82.32%)**. Both groups have 14 truncated responses, retained in the full denominator.
- The paired A5 runs differ only in the LM head option. These are single-run accuracy comparisons. Evaluation wall time also depends on generated token counts and is not reported as an isolated LM head speedup.

**Previous A2 serving performance validation**

Compared BF16 and INT8 target heads on Ascend 910B4, physical cards 4-7, TP4, using the same W8A8 checkpoint and the five-scenario `jiangli221/blue-green` PerfTest workflow (commit `0a8c2760938e248966a5a332a761e033d223a351`). Each scenario ran twice, with MTP K3, prefix caching, and `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`; independent draft heads remained BF16. Both groups used the same runtime configuration, including `fuse_norm_quant=false` for image compatibility.

Representative 8K-input/2K-output runs at concurrency 8 reduced TPOT by approximately **0.5-1 ms**: **19.336 to 18.411 ms (-0.925 ms)** in round 1 and **16.141 to 15.637 ms (-0.504 ms)** in round 2. Two-round means across all five scenarios are:

| Scenario | BF16 TPOT (ms) | INT8 TPOT (ms) | TPOT reduction (ms) | Output throughput change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8K/2K, concurrency 8, 64 requests | 17.739 | 17.024 | 0.715 | +5.71% |
| 20K/300, concurrency 4, 32 requests | 21.748 | 21.357 | 0.391 | +3.69% |
| `gsm8k64_c8`, concurrency 8, 64 requests | 18.060 | 17.576 | 0.484 | +3.17% |
| 24K/512, concurrency 8, 24 requests | 19.604 | 18.894 | 0.710 | +2.80% |
| 20K/300, concurrency 1, 8 requests | 10.018 | 9.803 | 0.215 | +2.38% |

These are historical A2 serving measurements, separate from the A5 accuracy runs above. Inputs were generated by PerfTest; its `gsm8k64_c8` scenario uses synthetic prompts rather than GSM8K benchmark questions. All requests succeeded, and client completion-token totals matched server metric deltas in all 20 rounds. TPOT was collected by the repository's SSE client as `(request_duration - TTFT) / (completion_tokens - 1)`. Per-rank head weight storage decreased from approximately 606.25 MiB to 303.125 MiB, excluding scales.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Added/updated tests for vocabulary padding, chunk boundaries, MX scale layouts, alternate head prefixes, missing configuration objects, and target/draft isolation.
- [x] **Regression test**: Added regressions for both review findings: silently skipped `head` prefixes and incomplete shared-embedding configuration checks.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Covered unsupported options/checkpoint recipes, missing metadata, incompatible methods, tied weights, unsupported weight dtypes, and V1 rejection.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Tests assert selected method identity, retained checkpoint behavior, loaded shard/bias data, and quantized tensor layouts and matmul arguments.
- [x] **Performance impact**: Completed paired A2 serving benchmarks with the PerfTest workflow. Representative runs reduced TPOT by approximately **0.5-1 ms**; the five-scenario means, throughput changes, and weight-memory reduction are recorded above. A2/A5 NPU correctness and paired model accuracy were also verified.

issues.title: [Feature] Support draft_lm_head_quantization (fp8) on Ascend NPU
issues.body:
## What this PR does / why we need it?

Brings the vLLM `draft_lm_head_quantization` feature (vLLM PR #59973) to Ascend NPU: the draft model's lm_head executes a **quantized copy of the shared target lm_head** instead of a bf16 copy, for `speculative_config.method ∈ {eagle, eagle3, mtp}`.

Ascend-specific execution selection (hardware-gated, no user toggles):

| Device class | Execution path |
|---|---|
| A5 / Ascend 950 (MXFP8-capable) | Native **MXFP8** matmul via the platform FP8 scaled-MM kernel |
| A3 / A2 / Ascend 910B (no MXFP8 hardware path) | **INT8 W8A8** kernel: PTPC e4m3 per-channel quantization at load, re-sampled to INT8 + per-channel scales |

Commits:
1. `vocab_parallel_embedding` op preparation (sharded quantized-head construction).
2. Draft lm_head fp8 support in the worker: share/restore of quantized lm heads across draft weight updates, incomplete-update tracking (mirrors GPUWorker), kernel registration `AscendFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel (MXFP8)` / `AscendFP8ScaledMMInt8LinearKernel (INT8)` with mutual gating.
3. INT8 execution for non-MXFP8 devices.
4. **BugFix**: on 910B, *every* e4m3 tensor copy/cast routes through `aclnnInplaceCopy`'s FP8-format path, which is unimplemented there (CANN error 561103) — so loading `draft_lm_head_quantization="fp8"` aborted on any 910B before this fix. The PTPC quantization and the INT8 re-sampling now move the e4m3 bytes through `uint8` views with CPU-side casts, producing **bit-identical weights**; runs once at model load (~seconds). MXFP8 devices keep the original in-device path.

`nvfp4` is rejected with a clear `ValueError` (needs CUDA W4A16 kernels).

Release-note fragment: `release_notes/fragments/19400.yaml` (feature + bugfix entries).

## Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

New: `speculative_config: {"method": "mtp", ..., "draft_lm_head_quantization": "fp8"}` now works on Ascend (vLLM v0.33.0 pairing). No new flags; execution format is picked per device. `nvfp4` raises an explicit unsupported error.

## How was this patch tested?

### Unit tests (added here, green on both device classes)

- `tests/ut/.../test_ascend_fp8_scaled_mm.py`: the unpatched PTPC path reproduces CANN **561103** on 910B; with the fix, e4m3 weights, INT8 re-quantized weights, and per-channel scales are **bit-identical to a CPU reference**. INT8 execution-path numerics covered as well.
- `tests/ut/test_platform.py`: `nvfp4` rejection.
- `tests/ut/ops/test_vocab_parallel_embedding.py`: op preparation.

### End-to-end validation (Qwen3.8-27B, MTP k=3, TP4, aisbench + frozen perf suite)

**A5 (Ascend 950DT, MXFP8 execution) — accuracy A/B** (identical stack, only the fp8 flag differs):

| Criterion | exp (fp8) | ctrl (bf16) | Bar | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Greedy output consistency (60-probe, temp=0) | **100% (60/60)** | — | ≥80% | PASS |
| Acceptance-length ratio | 2.93 | 2.99 | ≥90% (**97.99%**) | PASS |
| ceval weighted (1346 q) | 88.04 | 87.37 | — | +0.67 |
| aime2026 (30 q) | 33.33 | 36.67 | — | -3.34 (single problem flip) |
| GPQA diamond (198 q) | 69.70 | 71.21 | — | -1.51 (3 flips, within σ≈3.3%) |

**A5 perf A/B (TP4)** (frozen 5-scenario × 2-round suite, 384 audited requests, eager): all metrics within **±1.4%**; sole exception gsm8k TTFT +5.65% (baseline 0.18 s; that scenario's wall -3.96% and throughput +2.28%, i.e. net faster). → **no performance regression** on the MXFP8 path.

**A2 (Ascend 910B4, INT8 execution) — the bugfix target** (raw bf16 checkpoint):
- Service: 4/4 ranks log the quantized fp8 draft-lm_head copy; gsm8k smoke 2/2; MTP acceptance-length healthy.
- Accuracy A/B (same stack, only the fp8 flag differs):
  - MTP acceptance-length ratio **93.94%** (exp 2.79 vs ctrl 2.97; ≥90% bar: PASS)
  - GPQA diamond: exp 70.20 vs ctrl 69.70 → Δ**+0.50** (PASS)
  - aime2026: exp 36.67 vs ctrl 43.33 → Δ-6.67 = 2 problem flips on n=30 (within binomial noise, σ_diff≈12.7pp; A5 shows the same single-flip pattern on a passing run)
  - ceval (offline scorer bit-exact with the aisbench protocol): exp 88.19 pooled (1187/1346, 0 failed generations); ctrl completion pending
- Greedy consistency (60-probe, temp=0): 11.7% on this stack — **under investigation**. Divergence is confined to long-CoT generations (short outputs mostly identical) and, in every case examined, appears at a mid-CoT near-tie branch point where both continuations remain coherent; benchmark-level metrics are unaffected (GPQA/AL above). Two confounders must be ruled out before concluding: (a) the ctrl-side probe overlapped ~50 min with concurrent eval traffic on the same server (batch-composition nondeterminism), and (b) the stack's own run-to-run greedy reproducibility has not yet been measured with an idle-server re-probe. The identical probe on A5/MXFP8 is 100%. The clean re-probe result will be posted in this PR.
- A3 (910B3) is covered by the A2 validation: the non-MXFP8 branch is a single code path shared across the 910B family.

**Perf supplements tracked in this PR (in progress, data to follow):**
- A2 (910B4) TP4 perf A/B on the frozen suite.
- A5 TP1 / TP2 perf supplements (TP1 is expected to show the largest quantized-draft-head gain: no vocab-parallel sharding of lm_head on a single card; TP4 numbers above).
- A2 ctrl ceval completion + the clean idle-server greedy re-probe.

## Checklist

- Testing
  - [x] Boundary / edge-case coverage — non-MXFP8 device gating, e4m3-byte round-trips, nvfp4 rejection covered by unit tests.
  - [x] Regression test — the CANN 561103 reproducer (fails without the fix, bit-identical with it).
  - [x] Error / failure path coverage — unsupported method/quant raises explicit errors.
  - [x] Meaningful & reliable tests — bit-exact assertions vs CPU reference, not smoke-only.
  - [x] Performance impact — benchmark results attached (A5 TP4 above; A2 / TP1 / TP2 supplements tracked in this PR).

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enable MiniMax M3 auxiliary hidden-state capture for DSpark while preserving QuaRot alignment and independent unrotated draft vocabulary weights. Extend the shared MRV1/MRV2 policy to keep target and EAGLE/DSpark ordinary-attention K/V contiguous, based on #19530 by @zhaochuang001.

Dedicated sparse/indexer attention remains unchanged. Window sizes come from layer configuration and causality from runtime metadata. Decode graph workspace uses a per-request query-length bound; complete Q and request offsets are passed through, and longer prefill keeps its actual length. The package is optional; unsupported configurations retain the existing backend.

Update the Chinese deployment/evaluation tutorial. No tests-directory changes or changes to vllm_ascend/models/qwen3_dspark.py are included.

Track the bounded Ascend/A5 implementation of Qwen-Image-2.1 Q/K RMSNorm +
interleaved RoPE and native prefix-KV concatenation. The current path launches
the normalization and rotation separately, and BSND prefix concatenation
materializes storage that the NPU Attention backend transposes back to BNSD.

Related RFC: #8586, A1/A3. Existing implementation: #8017. This is the
Ascend-specific native-cache slice; it does not replace the GPU kernel or FP8
packing work in #7945/#7946, or claim those contributors' tasks.

## Proposed scope and acceptance

- Rebase #8017 onto current `main` and reuse the public
  `mindiesd.norm_rope_concat` API through `CustomOp`.
- Retain separate, default-off QKV and head-major concatenation settings.
- Preserve original prefix-cache writes, CFG branch isolation, masking, and
  cache representation; propagate execution errors after selecting the operator.
- Gate the first supported slice to A5/BF16/batch1/head_dim128/TP1/SP1/eager,
  unquantized weights and native KV; unsupported configurations retain the
  existing path with an observable reason.
- Verify configuration and portable dispatch, cached rotated-prefix ownership,
  layout values, real NPU numerical behavior, and full-request T2I/I2I.
- Report warmup, interleaved A/B samples, spread, memory, source/dependency
  identities and the fused BF16/RoPE rounding difference. A single-seed image
  screen is not formal quality acceptance.

Consumable MindIE-SD packaging, formal quality acceptance, and expansion to
other devices/dtypes/batches/parallelism/graphs/Turbo remain separate gates.
No startup compatibility workaround belongs in the optimization PR.

## Existing issue search

Searched the repository's Qwen-Image-2.1, gate, VAE-cache, and norm/RoPE reports
before filing. #8076 is broad model support; #8586 is the parent roadmap.
This issue gives #8017 a focused implementation/acceptance boundary.

issues.title: [RFC]: Qwen-Image 2.1 performance optimization — low-latency, high-throughput, and memory-efficient serving
issues.body:
## Motivation

Native `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` support is merged in [#8099](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8099). We would like community help to reduce generation latency and memory use, improve serving throughput, and turn the available optimizations into reproducible deployment recipes.

**Help wanted:** contributors with experience in kernels, attention, compilation, batching, quantization, distributed execution, or profiling are welcome. Hardware owners can contribute baseline runs, traces, quality comparisons, or reviews. Please pick a bounded item below and comment with your hardware and proposed scope so we can coordinate work.

This follows the community optimization trackers for [SenseNova-U1.5 (#7598)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/7598), [Ming-Image (#8134)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8134), and [MAGI-2 (#7085)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/7085). The serving goals are:

- **A — Low latency:** minimize single-request end-to-end latency and denoising time.
- **B — High throughput:** maximize successful images/s under concurrency while reporting p50/p95/p99 latency and failures.
- **C — Memory efficiency and hardware coverage:** qualify practical configurations for smaller GPUs and additional platforms, with their latency and quality costs recorded.

## Current baseline

Initial source snapshot: [`main` at `3dc35694`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/commit/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea). Contributors should record the exact SHA used for each comparison.

The model supports text-to-image and editing with up to four condition images. Request batching, step execution, TP/CFG parallelism, regional compilation, decode CUDA graphs, prefix KV reuse, online FP8, and VAE tiling already have implementation paths. Ulysses SP has partial validation; HSDP and layerwise offload remain marked unverified. Ring attention and pipeline parallelism are unsupported; TeaCache and Cache-DiT are under review ([#9199](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9199), [#9062](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9062)). LoRA is wired but lacks real-adapter end-to-end evidence.

Sources: [feature matrix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/docs/user_guide/diffusion_features.md), [recipe](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/recipes/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1.md), and [support PR validation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8099).

### Published measurements to reproduce

These are historical recipe measurements, not new benchmarks for this issue or universal performance targets. The support PR recorded vLLM 0.30.0, Torch 2.13.0+cu129, and Transformers 5.14.1. The H200 runs used the teapot prompt, 1024×1024, 50 steps, seed 42, and `true_cfg_scale=1.0`; new runs should use and record an environment compatible with their pinned Omni commit.

| Comparison | Configuration | Reported time/image | Quality / memory |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Compile/graph sweep; one warmup, median of three | Compile + graph | 5.93 s | 38.10 dB PSNR vs eager |
| Same sweep | Compile only | 6.88 s | 38.10 dB vs eager |
| Same sweep | Graph only | 9.52 s | Pixel-identical to eager |
| Same sweep | Eager | 8.28 s | Reference |
| Separate eager FP8 comparison | BF16 | 7.34 s | 36.9 GB peak |
| Same FP8 comparison | DiT FP8, all eligible layers | 6.06 s | 30.4 GB peak; 33.0 dB vs BF16 |

Do not combine the two sweeps into one speedup calculation. Graph-only was slower than eager in the published sweep; trace evidence should guide further capture work. Compilation and FP8 also require output-quality comparisons.

## Work items

Ownership updated on **November 7, 2026** from the linked volunteer replies. Every item now has an owner or a covered draft; per-row status links to first reports and open follow-ups. See the [initial coordination and requested cross-reviews](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6062985809) and the [November 7 status reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6703954311).

S/M/L indicate approximate scope, not promised effort or speedup. Existing PRs are in progress; coordinate with their authors before starting overlapping work.

### A — Low latency

| ID | Item | Scope | Status / starting point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A0 | Reproduce a baseline and profile text/image encoding, prefix prefill, denoising decode, VAE decode, and response encoding. Share traces and identify the largest measured cost. | S | Complete: [`luca-888`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6056840027). [Report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6061770135) independently rerun on a second H200 ([cross-review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6130580327)): pixel-identical outputs, latency within 1.2%, identical peak memory. Largest cost: denoising, 96–97% of end-to-end latency; GEMM ≈ half of kernel time, elementwise/copy/cast ≈ a third (~1,830 kernels/step). |
| A1 | Fuse or tune Q/K normalization + RoPE, SwiGLU, modulation, and residual operations; measure full-model impact and numerical behavior across GPU generations. | M | Owner: 0z5a via [#7945](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/7945); [plan](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6066223034) separates fusion and 0/6-layer residency variants for separate attribution. Cross-review and additional GPU generations still open |
| A2 | Tune attention and compile/graph execution for 1024/2048 outputs, longer prompts, and editing prefixes. Measure launch overhead, compile/capture cost, graph memory, and eager fallbacks. | M | Claimed: [`nagisa-kunhah`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6042015748). H20; attention and compile/graph profiling, optimization, and correctness validation. Existing compile/graph path; backend correctness must cover block-causal masking |
| A3 | Reduce prefix-KV dequantization, packing, and allocation overhead for long prompts and multi-image editing. | M | Claimed: [`YuDeng0102`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6051183607). A100 40GB; validation and coordinated follow-ups to #7946, whose implementation remains owned by 0z5a. Coordinate with [#7946](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/7946); preserve cache format and attention semantics |

### B — High throughput

| ID | Item | Scope | Status / starting point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | Benchmark and optimize existing request batching versus step execution at concurrency 1/2/4/8/16 where memory permits. Include staggered arrivals, mixed prefill/decode phases, cancellation, and sustained load. | M | First [report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6226309773) posted (A100-40GB, c=1/2/4/8 closed-loop, staggered, cancellation): request batching ≈ step execution at equal batch size; ≤ ~2.6% engine-throughput gain from batching at c=1; p50 rises 28–35% under staggered arrivals; cancellation is the main mode difference. No scheduler change proposed; sustained load remains open. [Shared B1/B2 workload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6226201142) |
| B2 | Profile editing batches with different prompt lengths and reference-image counts/sizes. Reduce padding, packing, and sub-batch overhead while preserving request order and conditioning isolation. | M | First [report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6233473228) posted (PRO6000, 14 workloads): mixed-length batches show larger output drift (27.66 dB worst case) than homogeneous batching; packing overhead measured small. Bounded change proposed: prompt (plus negative-prompt under true CFG) length in `batch_compatibility_key`, graph-enabled serving only; PR to follow against the shared B1/B2 workload |
| B3 | Compare TP/CFG/SP profiles with independent server replicas on the same total GPU budget. Qualify the best latency and throughput configurations separately. | M | Claimed: [`0z5a`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6067807970) on 8×H100. TP=2/4 H200 results exist and stay a separate cohort; true CFG, SP padding, and combinations need dedicated validation |

### C — Memory efficiency, hardware, and regression coverage

| ID | Item | Scope | Status / starting point |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Validate DiT FP8, text-encoder FP8, their combination, selective BF16 layers, and FP8 prefix storage across several prompts and editing inputs. Measure quality, latency, and peak memory. | S–M | First [comparison](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6130838641) posted (H200, 7 configurations: DiT/selective-BF16/text-encoder/prefix V and K+V FP8, multiple prompts and edit inputs), [revised per cross-review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6152303526) with a per-case LPIPS ≤ 0.15 gate and dB comparisons. DiT FP8: −16.8% T2I / −15.6% edit latency vs BF16, no recorded failures/OOMs. FP8 prefix storage follow-up stays coordinated with A3 |
| C2 | Qualify model-level/layerwise offload, selective residency, and VAE tiling at 1024/2048 on constrained VRAM. Report transfer cost and actual device peaks. | M | First [report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6142595428) posted (H100/5090/4090): offload+tiling runs all four cells at ≤ 22.69 GiB reserved on 24/32 GB; untiled VAE decode remains the offloaded limit. [#8680](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8680) merged: peak allocated 36.86 → 33.96 GiB at 1024², [edit row confirmed on H200](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6163716714). Recipe convention: peak reserved, per-hardware-cohort tables. Open: untiled 2048² decode under offload on 24/32 GB; residency variants with #7945 |
| C3 | Reproduce and diagnose consumer-GPU TP corruption, then qualify TP/SP/CFG and supported attention backends on additional hardware. | M | Claimed: [`fangfangssj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6108085424) on RTX 4090 / RTX 5090 / Ascend 910C: BF16 T2I baseline, attention backends, TP/SP/CFG qualification, and a #8135 repro attempt. [#8135](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8135): mixed RTX 5070/5070 Ti + WSL2 report; H200 did not reproduce it. Intel XPU enablement: [#8509](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8509). NPU AdaLN work: [#8005](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8005) |
| C4 | Provision the checkpoint for GPU CI, enable serving/quality tests that actually execute, and add repeatable performance baselines and qualified recipes. | S–M | Nightly 2.1 accuracy ([#8726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8726)) and perf ([#8923](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8923)) jobs landed. Remaining: the online e2e smoke test still skips without `QWEN_IMAGE_21_TEST_MODEL` and no CI job runs it — claimed: [`latioswang`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6658531002) (A100 80GB; ready-tier placement and checkpoint caching answered in the [November 7 status reply](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6703954311)) |

Cache approximation or fewer-step sampling proposals are welcome as separate experiments with explicit quality gates. TeaCache/Cache-DiT integration must account for the prefix prefill/decode split and calibrate against this model; copying older Qwen-Image coefficients does not establish compatibility. A lower step count or different CFG setting is a changed workload, not an isolated runtime speedup. In progress under these terms: [TeaCache #9199](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9199) (Qing7364) and [Cache-DiT #9062](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/9062) (nagisa-kunhah), with mutual cross-review requested.

## Evidence and acceptance criteria

Use the shared [diffusion serving benchmark](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/benchmarks/diffusion/diffusion_benchmark_serving.py) and [pipeline profiling guide](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/3dc35694b3d458fc1461a8fe71832ac12e8c8cea/docs/contributing/profiling.md) where applicable. Start with one bounded workload; expansion should follow measured bottlenecks.

- [ ] Record the hypothesis, isolated variable, fixed controls, success criterion, run budget, and stop condition before comparison. Pin repository/model revisions, local modifications, environment, hardware/device IDs, backend, inputs, precision, resolution, steps, CFG, and cache settings.
- [ ] Probe feasibility first. Default to one feasibility run and two additional measured runs per configuration; declare a different budget in advance when needed. Exclude preparation and warmups, report variation, and retain commands, raw results, profiler traces, and output images. Do not drop shared caches.
- [ ] Separate startup/download/compilation from process-to-readiness and steady serving. Keep readiness behavior fixed, validate the first inference after readiness, and reuse the prepared environment/server unless startup is the measured variable.
- [ ] Report client latency, engine/stage time, successful throughput, errors, and host/device memory as appropriate. Keep all failed/OOM cases visible; do not pool different hardware or workloads.
- [ ] For kernel, packing, scheduling, and parallelism changes, demonstrate numerical equivalence within a declared tolerance and correct conditioning/order. For FP8, approximate caching/attention, or sampling changes, declare quality tolerances before evaluation; compare against BF16/no-approximation with PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS and visual checks for typography, identity, edits, and RGBA transparency.
- [ ] Validate affected feature combinations and existing consumers of shared changes. Update recipes and feature cells only for configurations with evidence; establish performance regression thresholds after measuring variability.

## Claim a task

Comment with:

```text
Item ID:
Contribution: baseline / profiling / implementation / quality evaluation / review
Hardware: device model, memory, device count, interconnect
Proposed workload and scope:
Success criterion:
Existing issue / PR:
```

A single reproducible baseline, useful trace, correctness test, or negative result is a valuable contribution. Every main item now has an owner or a covered draft, so new volunteers should start from the open follow-ups listed per row (sustained-load serving in B1, FP8 prefix storage in C1/A3, fused-kernel attribution in A1, untiled 2048² decode under offload in C2). We can split claimed work into focused follow-up issues and keep ownership/results linked here.

Feedback is welcome for at least one week from filing; task claims remain open as work progresses.

issues.title: Qwen-Image-2.1: TP=2 output corrupted with dense chroma speckle (single-GPU clean; SGLang TP=2 shows the identical corruption)
issues.body:
### Summary

Qwen-Image-2.1 serving with `--tensor-parallel-size 2` (PR #7759 branch) produces images corrupted by **dense multicolored (chroma) speckle noise** across smooth regions, while image composition/structure remains correct. Single-GPU serving with the same code and the same local patches produces clean output. The official recipe itself lists "TP=2/4 output parity — pending measurement", and we can confirm: **TP=2 parity does not hold**.

We also reproduced the **identical corruption with SGLang's independent TP implementation** (sgl-project/sglang, diffusion path, `--tp-size 2`), and verified NCCL collective numerics across our mixed-GPU pair are clean — details below. This points to a shared flaw in how this model is sharded under TP (both engines use vLLM-style parallel-layer conventions), rather than a hardware or transport problem.

### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| GPUs | 2× RTX 5070 Ti (16GB) + RTX 5070 (12GB), both Blackwell `sm_120` |
| Driver / OS | Windows 11 + WSL2 (Ubuntu 24.04), latest NVIDIA driver |
| vLLM-Omni | PR #7759 branch, commit `3d6a1c4d` |
| vllm / torch | 0.29.0 / 2.13.0+cu130 |
| Model | Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 (bf16 weights) |

### Reproduce

```bash
vllm serve /root/models/Qwen-Image-2.1 --omni \
  --served-model-name qwen-image-2.1 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8091 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --diffusion-offload-config '{"mode":"layer","components":["text_encoder"],"pin_memory":false}' \
  --step-execution --max-num-seqs 1 --enforce-eager
```

```bash
curl http://localhost:8091/v1/images/generations -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model": "qwen-image-2.1",
  "prompt": "a ceramic teapot on a wooden table, soft window light, clean background",
  "size": "1024x1024",
  "num_inference_steps": 40,
  "true_cfg_scale": 1.0,
  "seed": 42
}'
```

Note: on 12–16GB consumer cards we run with a few local patches that keep the text encoder (Qwen3-VL 8B) and its `lm_head`/`embed_tokens` on CPU and pin the VAE to fp16 (the offload path PR #7759 ships assumes larger VRAM). **These patches are exonerated as the corruption source** — single-GPU serving with the exact same patched tree is clean.

### What the corruption looks like

- Dense green/purple/orange single-to-few-pixel speckles over smooth areas (walls, table, gradients); fine structure (edges, objects) preserved.
- Deterministic across seeds and prompts; present at 1024² and larger; present for both t2i and image editing.
- Not subtle — immediately visible; ~4-8% of pixels in flat regions show chroma noise in our pixel-diff quantification vs single-GPU output of the same seed.

### What we ruled out (evidence chain)

1. **VAE decode dtype** — VAE pinned to fp16 in all tests (bf16 decode has its own, different speckle signature); corruption unchanged. Excluded.
2. **Our local patches** — single-GPU run on the same patched tree is clean. Excluded.
3. **Rank order / mixed-GPU placement** — swapped the two different cards between rank 0/1; corruption identical. Excluded.
4. **NCCL transport / mixed GPU models** — wrote a `torch.distributed` test: bf16/fp16/fp32 all-reduce on both cards vs Gloo CPU fp64 reference. Max relative error: fp32 ≈ 4e-8, fp16 ≈ 3e-4 (≈ half-ulp), bf16 ≈ 2.5e-3 (exactly one bf16 ulp) — all normal rounding, no corruption; 50-round 4096² stress accumulation: zero NaN/Inf. Transport is numerically clean. Excluded.
5. **Engine-specific plumbing** — **SGLang** (sgl-project/sglang, main @ `8ab21c8a9`, `--model-type diffusion --tp-size 2`, flash-attn 2.8.3 self-built for sm_120, `--attention-backend fa2`) reproduces the **same speckle corruption at 1024²/30 steps**, while its single-GPU path with the same offload flags is clean. Two independent TP implementations failing with the same visual signature suggests the shared sharding recipe for this architecture is the problem.

### Suspects (for whoever picks this up)

Both engines shard this DiT with the standard vLLM parallel-layer conventions (QKV column-parallel / row-parallel FFN + all-reduce). Things specific to Qwen-Image-2.1 that interact with that recipe and are worth checking first:

- The single-stream joint text+image attention (32 single-stream blocks, structural block-causal masks) — per-rank mask/RoPE boundary handling with 16 heads per rank.
- Per-head QK-norm (`QwenImage21ZeroCenterRMSNorm`, fp32 computed, weight+1 trick) under head sharding.
- AdaLN modulation MLPs — if these are sharded+all-reduced like ordinary FFNs, partial shifts/scales get summed, which would produce exactly this class of mild, structure-preserving corruption.

### Artifacts

Happy to attach side-by-side PNGs (TP=2 vs single-GPU, same seed), pixel-diff maps, or the NCCL test script on request.

### Impact

TP=2 is the only way this model fits 2K (2752×1536) workloads on consumer GPUs; with the corruption it is unusable, and single-GPU caps out near ~1536px without DiT layerwise offload. A fix (or even identifying which layer is mis-sharded) would be very welcome.

## Summary

- Add opt-in MindIE-SD residual `mul + add` fusion for Qwen-Image-2.1 NPU decode, enabled with `extras={"qwen21_fuse_residual_gate": True}` (default: off).
- Preserve BF16 intermediate-product rounding and reuse the existing shared `tanh`.
- Apply to Attention and MLP residuals in unquantized BF16, batch-1, TP1/SP1 eager inference without LoRA, offload, or HSDP. Prefill and unsupported configurations retain the existing path.
- Add backend availability checks, fallback tests, and recipe documentation.

Requires [MindIE-SD commit 6198923](https://gitcode.com/HAAZZZEEEE/MindIE-SD/commit/6198923bcad4ec8909c2f263a3d3ff63b2316804), which adds the optional `preserve_mul_rounding` argument.

## Test results

Environment: Ascend950PR, PyTorch 2.10.0, torch-npu 2.10.0.post4, triton-ascend 3.2.2, vLLM 0.32.0.

- Omni unit tests: **4 passed**.
- MindIE-SD operator tests: **17 passed**.
- T2I/I2I smoke: 512×512, 4 steps, seed 42, CFG 1. All **384 residual comparisons were elementwise identical**; enabled/disabled output image hashes matched within each scenario.
- Applicable pre-commit checks passed. Omni actionlint was skipped after an environment download failure; no workflow files changed.

Operator A/B: BF16 `[1,S,4096]`, broadcast gate `[1,1,4096]`; 20 warmups and 50 interleaved samples per variant.

|---|---:|---:|
| 1024 | 21.104 | 64.632 |
| 4096 | 55.741 | 115.633 |
| 8192 | 150.919 | 213.628 |

The current fused call path is slower. NPU event timings may include host dispatch gaps and do not isolate kernel execution. Repeated 1024×1024, 50-step model A/B and profiling remain pending due to device availability.

## Contributor intent

Confirmed by the contributor:
1. **Outcome:** Add AlignCache support to vLLM-Omni.
2. **Key variable:** Reduce model forward passes while maintaining acceptable output quality.
3. **Approach:** Predict selected diffusion outputs using cached history, with validation and request isolation.
4. **Users:** Wan, Qwen-Image, and MiniMax-H3 users seeking faster generation.

## Purpose

Add a request-scoped `align_cache` backend for Wan2.1 T2V, Wan2.2 T2V-A14B/I2V-A14B/TI2V-5B, Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I, and MiniMax-H3 T2VA.

Preserve native scheduler steps, provide exact/trace/acceleration modes, validate supported configurations, and isolate cache state between requests. Include explicit Qwen online FP8 admission, client-facing admission errors, worker contract checks, regression tests, and documentation. Offload, including `kv_offload_config`, remains unsupported; native forwards preserve unrelated PyTorch dispatch modes.

Documentation: [AlignCache guide](https://github.com/Linorman/vllm-omni/blob/cd50a8343ba429649d679478749e741303656417/docs/user_guide/diffusion/cache_acceleration/aligncache.md) and the diffusion runtime design.

## Test Plan / Results

Tested native `841cb06be2a987c99bceb77abdede8e2ee3d5fc2` against head `cd50a8343ba429649d679478749e741303656417`. The two RTX 5090s ran independent single-GPU experiments, with matched inputs, seeds, timesteps, precision, and device across all four arms. Each case/arm used 2 warmups + 5 measured repetitions.

| Model / profile | Output H×W / frames | Steps / CFG | Precision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wan2.1 T2V-1.3B / `wan21_reference_v1` | 480×832 / 17 | 50 / 5 | BF16 |
| Wan2.2 TI2V-5B, no-image branch / `wan22_ti2v_reference_v1` | 320×576 / 17 | 50 / 5 | BF16 |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I / `qwen21_reference_v1` | 768×768 / 1 | 50 / 4 | Online FP8 + BF16 activations |

Checkpoint revisions: Wan2.1 `0fad780a534b6463e45facd96134c9f345acfa5b`; Wan2.2 `b8fff7315c768468a5333511427288870b2e9635`; Qwen `d26bb61231c349cf6b7896fa83353113880e1ba3`.

Wan2.1 and Qwen use profile defaults; Wan2.2 uses threshold **0.10**, feedback EMA **0.5**, ratio bounds **[0.5, 2.0]**, and feedback-scale bounds **[0.5, 1.5]** in all phases.

| Model / reported cases | Mean latency: native / none / exact / accelerate (s) | Speedup vs native / none | PSNR (dB) | Actual forwards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wan2.1 | 17.244 / 17.181 / 17.365 / 8.090 | 2.131× / 2.124× | 30.349 | 100→44 |
| Wan2.2 | 5.759 / 5.763 / 5.865 / 2.886 | 1.995× / 1.996× | 26.973 | 100→44 |
| Qwen | 11.378 / 11.375 / 11.731 / 4.505 | 2.526× / 2.525× | 31.728 | 100→34 |

All **50 scheduler steps** were retained. `none` and `force_exact` matched native outputs and latents exactly within `atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5`. PSNR is measured against paired native outputs; Qwen RGBA is consistently composited over white.

## Upstream integration update

Merged upstream `b1f11f181` into head `ae98842ac`. The H3 denoising loop retains upstream reference-KV lifecycle and `finally` cleanup alongside AlignCache prediction. AlignCache now rejects any configured `kv_offload_config` before model loading, during installation, and at request entry; `None` remains allowed.
